 Judgment

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Sub Inspector of Subramanyanagar police station against the accused no.1 to 4 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323,
504, 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC .
2.
In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that the accused no.1 married C.W.1 on 04.02.2018 at Vigneshwara Sabha Bhavana, Parkala, Udupi District as per hindu rites and customs.

After marriage when accused no.1 to 4 no.1 and C.W.1 were residing at No.3254/B, 3 rd floor, C block, 4th cross, Gayathringar, the accused no.1 to 4 no.1 used to come home late from work and when C.W.1 questioned the accused no.1 to 4 no.1, he picked up quarrel with C.W.1, assaulted and subjected her to physical cruelty.

When the C.W.1 complained about the acts of accused no.1 to her mother in law(accused no.2) she also abused C.W.1 in filthy language and the accused no.4 being the younger brother of accused no.1 was misbehaving with the C.W.1.

The accused no.3 being the maternal aunt of accused no.1 used to taunt C.W.1 saying that she had to obey the accused no.1 and used to say that the accused no.1 did not like her as his wife, as she is aged and insisted her to leave the accused no.1 and go to her parental house and threatened her with dire consequences.
The C.C.25273/2019 accused no.1 to 4 extended physical and mental harassament towards C.W.1 amd confined her in the house and locked the door of the house and went outside.
The C.W.1 unable to bear the harassment of the accused no.1 to 4 persons lodged a complaint before the Women Police Station at Udupi on 13.12.2018.

When the C.W.1 returned to her matrimonial house at Bengaluru, the accused no.1 to 4 persons had vacated the said house without even informing C.W.1 and taken away the belongings of C.W.1 with them, therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused no.1 to 4 before the Subramanyanagar Police seeking necessary action against him in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.66/2019 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused no.1 to 4 , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, subsequently in persuance of summons the accused no.1 to 4 appeared before this Court and were enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as Ujjala vs Bharath Krishnakumar K N on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91526076/

sentences.text:
After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused no.1 to 4 , therefore charge C.C.25273/2019 was framed and read over and explained to the accused no.1 to 4 in the language known to him, after understanding the same he denied the same and claimed to be tried,
accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused no.1 to 4 , as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 10 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused no.1 to 4 as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.

6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused no.1 to 4 .
7.

In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused no.1 married C.W.1 on 04.02.2018 at Vigneshwara Sabha Bhavana, Parkala,
Udupi District as per hindu rites and customs.

After marriage when accused no.1 to 4 no.1 and C.W.1 were residing at No.3254/B, 3rd floor, C block, 4th cross,
Gayathringar, the accused no.1 to 4 no.1 used to come home late from work and when C.W.1 questioned the accused no.1 to 4 no.1, he picked up quarrel with C.W.1,
assaulted and subjected her to physical cruelty.

When the C.W.1 complained about the acts of accused no.1 to her mother in law(accused no.2) she also abused C.W.1 in filthy language and the accused no.4 being the younger brother of accused no.1 C.C.25273/2019 was misbehaving with the C.W.1.

The accused no.3 being the maternal aunt of accused no.1 used to taunt C.W.1 saying that she had to obey the accused no.1 and used to say that the accused no.1 did not like her as his wife, as she is aged and insisted her to leave the accused no.1 and go to her parental house and threatened her with dire consequences.

The accused no.1 to 4 extended physical and mental harassament towards C.W.1 amd confined her in the house and locked the door of the house and went outside thereby the accused no.1 to 4 have committed an offence punishable under section 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while the C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 4 at the matrimonial house, the accused no.1 to 4 abused C.W.1 in filthy language knowingly that it would give provocation to C.W.1 to breach public peace and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 committed the offence of "intentional insult"
Ujjala vs Bharath Krishnakumar K N on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91526076/
3 punishable U/s 504 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while the C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 4 at the matrimonial house, the accused no.1 to 4 without any provocation assaulted C.W.1 and caused hurt and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 has committed an offence of "voluntarily causing hurt"punishable U/s 323 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that accused no.1 to 4 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention, criminally intimidated to the life of C.W1 and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 have committed C.C.25273/2019 an offence of "criminal intimidation" punishable U/s 506 r/w Sec.34 OF IPC?
5. What Order?
8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 4 : In the 'Negative' Point No.5 : As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 to 4 : These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.

sentences.text: 10. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

The C.W.1 being complainant as well as victim in this case is examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1 and 2 documents got marked on her behalf, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Ujwala and she deposed in her evidence that accused no.1 is her husband and her marriage was solemnized with the accused no.1 on 04.02.2018 at Parkala, Udupa.

Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused no.1 she was residing at the matrimonial house with the accused no.1 to 4 and she was living with together in cordial terms and the accused no.1 to 4 persons did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused no.1 to 4.

She deposed that when she had been to Udupi P.S in the year 2019 police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 C.C.25273/2019 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

sentences.text: As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.

So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused no.1 to 4 persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused no.1 to 4 however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 4 , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 4 beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused no.1 to 4 ,
for which I answer point Nos.1 to 6 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.7:

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 4 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
C.C.25273/2019 ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused no.1 to 4 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A, 323, 504, 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC .
The bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 4 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 4 are ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 01st day of September, 2025.)
